ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير وأبو ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Jubayr, and Abū Maysara identify the lasting righteous deeds as the five daily prayers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وابن جبير وأبو ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل هي الصلوات الخمس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r2.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās includes every good word or deed that endures into the afterlife; al-Ṭabarī prefers this view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه كل عمل صالح من قول أو فعل يبقى للآخرة، ورجحه الطبري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r3.claim: The broad interpretation held by most is transmitted from the Prophet through Abū Hurayra and others.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r3.anchor: وقول الجمهور مروي عن الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم من طريق أبي هريرة وغيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r4.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r4.claim: Qatāda interprets the lasting deeds as everything done seeking God's face.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r4.anchor: وعن قتادة: كل ما أريد به وجه الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r5.speaker: الحسن وابن عطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Ibn ʿAṭāʾ identify them as good intentions, through which deeds are accepted and raised.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r5.anchor: وعن الحسن وابن عطاء: أنها النيات الصالحة فإن بها تتقبل الأعمال وترفع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r6.claim: They are better in reward because they endure, whereas worldly goods perish; what lasts is better than what passes away.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r6.anchor: ومعنى خير عند ربك ثوابا أنها دائمة باقية وخيرات الدنيا منقرضة فانية، والدائم الباقي خير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r7.claim: They are better in hope because their practitioner expects God's reward in the next life, unlike someone with only wealth and children.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p186/r7.anchor: وخير أملا أي وخير رجاء لأن صاحبها يأمل في الدنيا ثواب الله ونصيبه في الآخرة

FARRA:v2p145/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p145/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p145/r8.claim: الباقيات الصالحات is interpreted either as the five prayers or as the formulas of glorifying, praising, declaring God's oneness, and magnifying Him.
FARRA:v2p145/r8.anchor: يقال هي الصلوات الخمس ويقال هي سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله

MAJAZ:v1p404/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p404/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p404/r6.claim: Hashīman means dry, crumbling plant matter; Labīd's verse uses it for dry branches.
MAJAZ:v1p404/r6.anchor:
«هشيما» (46) أي يابسا متفتتا [قال لبيد:
ولا للضيف إن طرقت بليل ... بأفنان العضاة وبالهشيم]

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174/r7.claim: Wealth and children, which ʿUtba and his rich companions boast about, are worldly adornment rather than provision for the Hereafter.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174/r7.anchor: {المال والبنون} التي يفتخر بها عتبة وأصحابه الأغنياء {زينة الحياة الدنيا} ليست من زاد الآخرة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174/r8.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174/r8.claim: He calls wealth and children the crop of this world and righteous deeds the crop of the Hereafter, though God may grant both to some.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174/r8.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه: المال والبنون حرث الدنيا والأعمال الصالحة حرث الآخرة وقد يجمعها الله لأقوام

BIQAI-FULL:v4p471/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p471/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p471/r6.claim: Wealth and children are the greatest worldly adornments, yet they decay quickly, require effort, and may bring good if used to please God or become harm and disappointment.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p471/r6.anchor: وهما أجل ما في هذه الدار من متاعها

BIQAI-FULL:v4p471/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p471/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p471/r7.claim: The enduring righteous deeds are good works done solely for God’s sake, which the author says he has urged earlier.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p471/r7.anchor: وهي أعمال الخير المجردة التي يقصد بها وجه الله تعالى التي رغبنا فيها

DURR-FULL:v5p394/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p394/r10.speaker: سفيان الثوري
DURR-FULL:v5p394/r10.claim: A saying attributed to Sufyan says money is so called because it turns people, and the world because it is near.
DURR-FULL:v5p394/r10.anchor: عن سفيان الثوري قال: كان يقال إنما سمي المال لأنه يميل بالناس وإنما سميت الدنيا لأنها دنت

DURR-FULL:v5p394/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p394/r11.speaker: عياض بن عقبة
DURR-FULL:v5p394/r11.claim: As his son Yahya was buried, a man consoled Iyad by saying his son had been a leader of the army and urging him to seek God's reward.
DURR-FULL:v5p394/r11.anchor: عن عياض بن عقبة أنه مات له ابن يقال له يحيى فلما نزل في قبره قال له رجل: والله إن كان لسيد الجيش فاحتسبه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p519#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p519#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p519#2/r9.claim: Calling wealth and children adornment is qualified by the parable's belittling context: they adorn this devalued life and should not become one's chief desire.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p519#2/r9.anchor: إنما المال والبنون زينة هذه الحياة المحقرة، فلا تتبعوها نفوسكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p519#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p519#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p519#2/r10.claim: Zina is a verbal noun predicated of concrete persons, so an omitted description must be supplied; the excerpt breaks off before giving it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p519#2/r10.anchor: وقوله زينة مصدر، وقد أخبر به عن أشخاص فإما أن يكون على تقدير محذوف، وتقديره:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p520#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p520#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p520#2/r1.claim: The segment's fragment glosses a term as what is left by a flood, then shifts into the wording about presentation in rows.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p520#2/r1.anchor: الترك، ومنه غدير الماء، وهو ما تركه السيل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p161#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p161#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p161#2/r1.claim: Wealth and children adorn worldly life (3:14), but assets and offspring are a trial (64:15); turning to God and worshipping Him is better than being occupied with them, collecting more, or excessively worrying for them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p161#2/r1.anchor: الإقبال عليه والتفرغ لعبادته، خير لكم من اشتغالكم بهم والجمع لهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p161#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p161#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p161#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and other early authorities identify the lasting righteous deeds as the five daily prayers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p161#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وسعيد بن جبير، وغير واحد من السلف: "الباقيات الصالحات" الصلوات الخمس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p161#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p161#2/r3.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح وسعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p161#2/r3.claim: Another report from Ata and Sa'id, citing Ibn Abbas, identifies them as the formulas: glory be to God, praise be to God, no deity but God, and God is greatest.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p161#2/r3.anchor: وقال عطاء بن أبي رباح، وسعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس: "الباقيات الصالحات" سبحان الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p161#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p161#2/r4.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p161#2/r4.claim: Uthman says they are the four remembrance formulas plus no might or power except through God; in Ahmad's report he explains this after describing forgiveness through the five prayers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p161#2/r4.anchor: فقال: هي (5) لا إله إلا الله، وسبحان الله، والحمد لله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r1.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r1.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib identifies the lasting deeds as the four remembrance formulas plus no might or power except through God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r1.anchor: قال: "الباقيات الصالحات" سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r2.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r2.claim: When offered prayer and fasting, then zakat and pilgrimage, Sa'id rejects both lists and says the five lasting formulas are the four remembrances plus no might or power except through God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r2.anchor: قال (6) لم تصب. فقلت: الزكاة والحج. فقال: لم تصب، ولكنهن الكلمات الخمس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r3.claim: Ibn Umar identifies them as no deity but God, God is greatest, glory be to God, and no might or power except through God; Ata is reported to give the same answer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r3.anchor: أنه سأل ابن عمر عن: {الباقيات الصالحات} قال: لا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r4.claim: Mujahid identifies them as glory be to God, praise be to God, no deity but God, and God is greatest.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {الباقيات الصالحات} سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r5.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r5.claim: Hasan and Qatada give the four formulas: no deity but God, God is greatest, praise be to God, and glory be to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r5.anchor: وقال عبد الرزاق: أخبرنا معمر، عن الحسن وقتادة في قوله: "الباقيات الصالحات"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r6.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r6.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says that glory be to God, praise be to God, no deity but God, and God is greatest are among the lasting righteous deeds; Ibn Jarir transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر، من الباقيات الصالحات"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r7.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r7.claim: The Prophet urges people to increase the lasting righteous deeds; asked what they are, he names the religion and explains it as magnifying, declaring God's oneness, glorifying and praising Him, and saying no might or power except through God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162/r7.anchor: قيل: وما هي (9) يا رسول الله؟ قال: "الملة"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162#2/r1.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162#2/r1.claim: Ahmad also transmits the Prophet's report, through Darraj, that people should increase the lasting righteous deeds and that they are the formulas of remembrance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162#2/r1.anchor: وهكذا رواه أحمد، من حديث دراج، به (10) .

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162#2/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162#2/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b includes no might or power except through God among the lasting deeds; Salim questions its inclusion, but Muhammad persists, and Salim confirms after citing Abu Ayyub's report that Abraham told the Prophet to teach the community this as a seed of Paradise because its soil is good and broad.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162#2/r2.anchor: فقال: لا إله إلا الله، وسبحان الله، والله أكبر، ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162#2/r3.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162#2/r3.claim: A report from Abu Ayyub says that during the heavenly ascent Abraham urged the Prophet to tell his community to plant abundantly in Paradise, explaining that its planting is no might or power except through God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162#2/r3.anchor: فأريت إبراهيم عليه السلام، فقال: يا جبريل من هذا معك؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162#2/r4.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162#2/r4.claim: A report from an unnamed man of the Ansar says the Prophet warned that supporting unjust rulers and believing their lies disowns one from him, while refusing both aligns one with him; he then names four remembrance formulas as the lasting righteous deeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162#2/r4.anchor: خرج علينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ونحن في المسجد بعد صلاة العشاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162#2/r5.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162#2/r5.claim: The Prophet names four remembrance formulas and a parent who loses a righteous child and seeks God's reward among five weighty deeds; he also names five beliefs with which one meets God and enters Paradise: God, the Last Day, Paradise, Hell, resurrection, and reckoning.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p162#2/r5.anchor: بخ بخ لخمس ما أثقلهن في الميزان: لا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p163/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p163/r1.speaker: شداد بن أوس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p163/r1.claim: Shaddad regrets asking his servant for a knife to play with, saying that since embracing Islam he had controlled every word except that one; he relays the Prophet's counsel to treasure a supplication for steadfastness, resolve in guidance, gratitude, worship, a sound heart and truthful tongue, good known to God, refuge from known evil, and forgiveness, when others hoard gold and silver. Ahmad and al-Nasa'i transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p163/r1.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "إذا كنز الناس الذهب والفضة فاكنزوا (14) هؤلاء الكلمات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p163/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p163/r2.speaker: سعد بن جنادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p163/r2.claim: Sa'd ibn Janadah says that after he first came to the Prophet from Taif and converted, the Prophet taught him the four remembrance formulas as lasting righteous deeds; al-Tabarani transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p163/r2.anchor: وعلمني هؤلاء الكلمات: سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p163/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p163/r3.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p163/r3.claim: A report through Sa'd ibn Janadah says that one who rises at night, performs ablution and rinses his mouth, then says each of the four formulas one hundred times is forgiven all sins except bloodshed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p163/r3.anchor: من قام من الليل فتوضأ ومضمض فاه، ثم قال: سبحان الله مائة مرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p163/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p163/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p163/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas gives a broad list of lasting deeds: remembrance, blessings on the Prophet, fasting, prayer, pilgrimage, charity, freeing slaves, jihad, maintaining kinship, and all good works, which remain for their people in Paradise as long as heaven and earth endure.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p163/r4.anchor: هي ذكر الله، قول: لا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p164/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p164/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p164/r1.claim: Al-Awfi transmits Ibn Abbas's interpretation of the lasting righteous deeds as good speech.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p164/r1.anchor: وقال العوفي، عن ابن عباس: هن الكلام الطيب.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p164/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p164/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p164/r2.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam says they are all righteous deeds; Ibn Jarir chooses this broad interpretation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p164/r2.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: هي الأعمال الصالحة كلها. واختاره ابن جرير

JISHUMI:v6p4423/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4423/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4423/r1.claim: The comparative خير ثوابا may answer ignorant claims that another can reward: even hypothetically, God would be best; alternatively, it compares the recompense for deeds without requiring a real rival.
JISHUMI:v6p4423/r1.anchor: قلنا: فيه وجهان: أحدهما: على ادعاء الجهال أنه يثيب غير الله

JISHUMI:v6p4423/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4423/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4423/r6.claim: Thawab means recompense and derives from returning; hope and expectation are near synonyms.
JISHUMI:v6p4423/r6.anchor: والثواب: الجزاء، وأصله من ثاب يثوب إذا رجع. والأمل والرجاء نظيران

JISHUMI:v6p4423/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4423/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4423/r8.claim: ثوابا and أملا are accusative specifications; هشيما is the predicate of أصبح with النبات omitted as its subject.
JISHUMI:v6p4423/r8.anchor: ثوابا، وأملا نصب على التمييز، هشيما خبر (أصبح) واسمه محذوف

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r7.claim: Wealth brings beauty and benefit, while sons bring strength and defense; together they adorn life.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r7.anchor: لأن في المال جمالا ونفعا وفي { البنين } قوة ودفعا فصارا زينة الحياة الدنيا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r8.claim: The abiding good deeds are the five prescribed prayers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r8.anchor: أنها الصلوات الخمس , قاله ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r9.anchor: أنها الأعمال الصالحة , قاله ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r10.speaker: ابن عباس وعطية العوفي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r10.claim: They are good words or speech.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r10.anchor: هي الكلام الطيب . وهذا مروي عن ابن عباس أيضا , وقاله عطية العوفي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r11.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r11.claim: They are phrases of glorification, praise, divine unity, greatness, and reliance on God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r11.anchor: هو قول سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر ولا حول ولا قوة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r12.speaker: أبو هريرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r12.claim: He reports the Prophet identifying glorification, praise, divine unity, and greatness as abiding good deeds.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r12.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر هي الباقيات الصالحات )

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r13.claim: Al-ṣāliḥāt may mean righteous agents, since a righteous person performs right action.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r13.anchor: أنها بمعنى الصالحين لأن الصالح هو فاعل الصلاح

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r14.claim: Alternatively, ṣāliḥāt means beneficial things, naming benefit by its soundness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r14.anchor: أنها بمعنى النافعات فعبر عن المنفعة بالصلاح

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r15.speaker: النبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r15.claim: During the Ascension, Abraham urged him to tell the community to plant Paradise abundantly; its soil is good and vast.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r15.anchor: لما عرج بي إلى السماء أريت إبراهيم فقال : مر أمتك أن يكثروا من غراس الجنة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r16.speaker: النبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r16.claim: Asked what Paradise's planting is, Abraham answered that there is no power or strength except through God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r16.anchor: فقلت وما غراس الجنة ؟ قال : لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p309/r17.claim: The reward is better with God in the Hereafter; hope is truer and better for oneself in this world.

MUQATIL:18:45-46/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:45-46/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:45-46/r3.claim: Wealth and children beautify worldly life, while enduring righteous deeds are better in reward and hope with God in the Hereafter.
MUQATIL:18:45-46/r3.anchor: يعنى: سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر،

MUQATIL:18:45-46/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:45-46/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:45-46/r4.claim: The enduring righteous deeds are saying glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is greatest.
MUQATIL:18:45-46/r4.anchor: يعنى: سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر،

MUQATIL:18:45-46/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:45-46/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:18:45-46/r5.claim: A report from the Prophet identifies the enduring righteous deeds as the four phrases of glorification, praise, monotheism, and magnification.
MUQATIL:18:45-46/r5.anchor: حدثنا عبيد الله، قال: حدثني أبي، عن الهذيل، عن مقاتل بن سليمان، عن علقمة بن مرثد وغيره، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r3.claim: The sūrah has three main narratives—the cave youths, Moses and the mysterious servant, and Dhu’l-Qarnayn—and a long parable warning against worldly enjoyment without gratitude and concern for the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r3.anchor: This sūrah contains three main narratives—that of the inhabitants of the cave

TABATABAI:18:45-46/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:45-46/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:45-46/r4.claim: Wealth and children are alluring but transient and cannot fulfill most hopes; this conclusion returns to the opening claim that earthly things were made as adornment.
TABATABAI:18:45-46/r4.anchor: لكنها زينة سريعة الزوال غارة لا يسعها أن تثيبه

TABATABAI:18:45-46/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:45-46/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:45-46/r5.claim: “The lasting good deeds” are righteous acts preserved by God; they bring better reward and truer hope because divine mercy and honor are attainable, unlike worldly hopes that mostly deceive.
TABATABAI:18:45-46/r5.anchor: المراد بالباقيات الصالحات الأعمال الصالحة فإن أعمال الإنسان محفوظة له عند الله

TABATABAI:18:45-46/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:45-46/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:45-46/r6.claim: Reports from the Prophet and the Imams identify the lasting good deeds as the four glorifications, prayer, or love of the Prophet’s family; the author treats these as applications to instances.
TABATABAI:18:45-46/r6.anchor: أن الباقيات الصالحات التسبيحات الأربع سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر

THALABI:v6p173/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p173/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p173/r1.claim: The wealth and children Uyayna and other elite rich people boast about adorn worldly life, but do not supply the grave or the afterlife.
THALABI:v6p173/r1.anchor: المال والبنون التي يفخر بها عيينة وأصحابه من الأشراف والأغنياء زينة الحياة الدنيا

THALABI:v6p173/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p173/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p173/r2.claim: The lasting good deeds of Salman and his poor companions are better in reward and hope.
THALABI:v6p173/r2.anchor: والباقيات الصالحات التي يعملها سلمان وأصحابه من الموالي والفقراء خير عند ربك ثوابا

THALABI:v6p173/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p173/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة ومجاهد والضحاك
THALABI:v6p173/r3.claim: They identify the lasting good deeds as saying tasbih, tahmid, tahlil, and takbir.
THALABI:v6p173/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس وعكرمة ومجاهد والضحاك: هي قول العبد

THALABI:v6p173/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p173/r4.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v6p173/r4.claim: A report from the Prophet says the four glorifications make a Muslim's sins fall away and are treasures of Paradise and lasting good words.
THALABI:v6p173/r4.anchor: إن المسلم إذا قال: سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر، تحاتت عنه الذنوب

THALABI:v6p173/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p173/r5.speaker: عثمان وابن عمر وسعيد بن المسيب وعطاء بن أبي رباح
THALABI:v6p173/r5.claim: They include لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله in the lasting good deeds, alongside the four formulas.
THALABI:v6p173/r5.anchor: وقال عثمان (رضي الله عنه) وابن عمر وسعيد بن المسيب وعطاء بن أبي رباح: هي

THALABI:v6p173/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p173/r6.speaker: خالد بن عمران
THALABI:v6p173/r6.claim: A report from the Prophet calls the five formulas a shield from the Fire and says they will surround their reciter on Judgment Day.
THALABI:v6p173/r6.anchor: فإنهن يأتين يوم القيامة مقدمات مجنبات ومعقبات، وهن الباقيات الصالحات

THALABI:v6p173/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p173/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
THALABI:v6p173/r7.claim: The Prophet urges people to increase the lasting good deeds and identifies them as takbir, tahlil, tasbih, and hawqala.

THALABI:v6p173/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p173/r8.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
THALABI:v6p173/r8.claim: Asked by Salim what the lasting deeds are, he lists the four formulas plus hawqala.
THALABI:v6p173/r8.anchor: فقال: لا إله إلا الله، والحمد لله، وسبحان الله، والله أكبر، ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله

THALABI:v6p173/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p173/r9.speaker: سالم
THALABI:v6p173/r9.claim: He challenges Muhammad ibn Ka'b about when hawqala was added to the list; the excerpt ends before the answer.
THALABI:v6p173/r9.anchor: فقال له سالم: متى جعلت: ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:45-46/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:45-46/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:45-46/r3.claim: Wealth and children are adornments of worldly life but do not benefit people in the afterlife; this rebuts leaders who boasted of them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:45-46/r3.anchor: هذا رد على الرؤساء الذين كانوا يفتخرون بالمال والأبناء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:45-46/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:45-46/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:45-46/r4.claim: Enduring righteous deeds mean the prayers, remembrances, and good works of Salman, Suhayb, and poor Muslims; they bring better reward and hope than wealth and children.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:45-46/r4.anchor: ما يأتي به سلمان وصهيب وفقراء المسلمين من الصلوات والأذكار والأعمال الصالحة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p188/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p188/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p188/r9.claim: The lasting righteous deeds are the five prayers; ʿAlī says they are the four declarations of praise, and others combine both views, attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p188/r9.anchor: قوله:} المال والبنون زينة الحياة الدنيا والباقيات الصالحات [الكهف: 46] الصلوات الخمس.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:45/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:45/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:45/r1.claim: Some wealthy Meccans, proud of property and sons, rejected monotheism and claimed life was only worldly; the verse compares transient worldly life to flourishing vegetation that soon dries and scatters.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:45/r1.anchor: Mekkeli bazı zenginler, mallarının ve oğullarının çokluğu sebebiyle şımardıkları için tevhid dinine girmeye tenezzül etmiyor

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:45/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:45/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:45/r2.claim: Worldly life is fleeting and wealth and children are its adornment; these pass away, while righteous deeds endure.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:45/r2.anchor: insanları aldatan dünya hayatı fânidir, mal ve çocuklar da bu dünyanın süsüdür; kısa bir süre sonra fâni olan gidecek, sâlih amel kalacaktır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:45/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:45/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:45/r3.claim: Righteous deeds include faith, morally good conduct, and all acts Islam commands or approves, including worship, striving, enjoining good, and kindness to parents, relatives, and neighbors.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:45/r3.anchor: sâlihât hem inanmayı hem de İslâm’ın yapılmasını emrettiği ve hoş karşıladığı, ahlâkî değerlere uygun işleri ve güzel davranışları ifade etmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:45/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:45/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:45/r4.claim: Islam permits lawful earning and enjoying good things; verse 7:32 says adornments and pure provisions are not forbidden and belong to believers in the next life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:45/r4.anchor: İslâm, helâl mal kazanmayı ve dünya nimetlerinden istifade etmeyi de yasaklamamıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:45/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:45/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:45/r5.claim: Islam disapproves of using blessings as grounds for arrogance toward the poor or as material and psychological pressure.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:45/r5.anchor: bu nimetlerin fakirlere karşı kibir ve gurur vesilesi edilmesini, maddî ve psikolojik baskı aracı yapılmasını hoş görmez.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The next parable addresses people blinded by love of worldly life: its ornaments will not accompany them to the next world; only righteous deeds endure as what they can earn.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: none of the adornments of this world will go with them to the next world. Only their righteous deeds will. So anyone who has to earn anything should do righteous deeds.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: In Arabia, tribal and family backing made children a source of strength, and people displayed their numbers in gatherings to assert superiority.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: in Arabia, the defence and power of a person depended on familial and tribal support, his strength depended on an abundance of children.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: A person should place hope in lasting righteous deeds, which bring eternal blessings.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The verse states that if a person has to pin hopes on it should be righteous deeds. They will reap eternal blessings for him.

BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r1.claim: “Remaining good deeds” is a noun for lasting acts of good, including prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, and words of glorification and praise.
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r1.anchor: {والباقيات الصالحات} الباقيات اسم لأعمال الخير لا وصف ولذا لم يذكر الموصوف

BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r2.claim: The Prophet calls people to take a shield against the Fire; the shield is saying the standard phrases of remembrance.
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r2.anchor: روي أنه عليه السلام خرج على قومه فقال : "خذوا جنتكم" قالوا : يا رسول الله أمن عدو حضر

BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r3.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r3.claim: Al-Kashifi reports that some scholars interpret the lasting good deeds as daughters, whose good upbringing can save parents from the Fire.
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r3.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (بعض علما برانندكه باقيات صالحات بنات است

BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r4.claim: A Prophetic report promises a shield from the Fire to whoever is tested with daughters and treats them well; beneficence should be understood broadly.
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r4.anchor: "من هذه البنات بشيء" من بيانية مع مجرورها حال من شيء "فأحسن إليهن"

BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r5.claim: The lasting deeds are better than perishable wealth and children: their reward returns to the person, and they fulfill hopes that worldly possessions cannot.
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r5.anchor: {خير} من الفانيات الفاسدات من المال والبنين {عند ربك} أي : في الآخرة {ثوابا} عائدة تعود إلى صاحبها

BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r6.claim: The verse rebukes boasting in worldly adornment; escape requires inward knowledge, love, and longing plus outward service, dignity, and high aspiration.
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r6.anchor: والآية تزهيد للمؤمنين في زينة الحياة الدنيا الفانية وتوبيخ للمفتخرين بها

BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r7.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r7.claim: Some say salvation from worldly adornment requires inward beauty through knowledge and love and outward beauty through service and noble aspiration.
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r7.anchor: لا ينجو من زينة الحياة الدنيا إلا من كان باطنه مزينا بأنوار المعرفة

BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r8.speaker: الضحاك
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits the Prophet’s description of the most ascetic person as one who remembers death, abandons excess, chooses what lasts, and counts himself among the dead.
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r8.anchor: وعن الضحاك عن النبي عليه السلام أنه قيل : يا رسول الله من أزهد الناس؟

BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r9.claim: A divine report says worldly increase distances a believer from God, while restriction brings the believer nearer; the Prophet recites 23:55–56 as evidence that abundance is a trial.
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r9.anchor: يفرح عبدي المؤمن إذا بسطت له شيئا من الدنيا وذلك أبعد له مني

BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r10.claim: The cited verses explain that God’s apparent increase in wealth and children may be a trial rather than a sign of good.
BURSEVI:v5p193#4/r10.anchor: {أيحسبون أنما نمدهم به من مال وبنين * نسارع لهم فى الخيراتا بل لا يشعرون}

QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r2.claim: Those who rely on possessions and children and forget their Lord lose in this life and regret what they missed in the next.
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r2.anchor: من اعتضد بعتاده ، واغتر بأولاده ، ونسي مولاه في أوان غفلاته

QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r3.claim: Money and sons adorn the heedless, while good works and certainty adorn those joined to God; the former rely on outward display, the latter on worship and knowledge of God.
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r3.anchor: زينة أهل الغفلة في الدنيا بالمال والبنين ، وزينة أهل الوصلة بالأعمال واليقين

QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r4.claim: Whatever gives the self a share is worldly adornment, including status, praise, and familiar attachments.
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r4.anchor: ما كان للنفس فيه حظ فهو منزينة الحياة الدنيا

QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r5.claim: Anything in which a person has a share is defective, whether its consequence arrives now or later.
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r5.anchor: ما كان للإنسان فيه شرب ونصيب فهو معلول

QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r6.claim: The lasting righteous works are actions marked by sincerity and truthfulness.
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r6.anchor: وهي الأعمال التي بشواهد الإخلاص والصدق

QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r7.claim: One interpretation defines lasting good works as deeds done purely for God, without desire or ulterior purpose.
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r7.anchor: ما كان خالصا لله تعالى غير مشوب بطمع ، ولا مصحوب بغرض

QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r8.claim: Another interpretation makes them divine qualities adorning inward secrets and sending their fragrance through the heavenly realm.
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r8.anchor: ما يلوح في السرائر من تحلية العبد بالنعوت ، ويفوح نشره في سماء الملكوت

QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r9.claim: Another interpretation sees them as nearness and noble intimacy already granted to a person from the unseen.
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r9.anchor: هي التي سبقت من الغيب له بالقربة وشريف الزلفة

QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r10.claim: Another interpretation calls them the lights of monotheism hidden in the heart, beyond the eclipse of veiling.
QUSHAYRI:v2p221/r10.anchor: ضياء شموس التوحيد المستكن في السرائر مما لا يتعرض لكسوف الحجبة

SULAMI:v1p410#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p410#5/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p410#5/r1.claim: Family, wealth, and children are the soul's worldly attachments, while the spirit's attachments are reliance, tranquility, trust, and certainty.
SULAMI:v1p410#5/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : المألوفات من الأهل والمال . والأولاد كلها من زينة الحياة الدنيا

SULAMI:v1p410#5/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p410#5/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p410#5/r2.claim: Only those adorned inwardly with gnosis, love, and longing and outwardly with service and noble aspiration escape worldly adornment and witness their King in nearness.
SULAMI:v1p410#5/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم : لا ينجو من زينة الحياة الدنيا إلا من كان باطنه مزينا بأنوار المعرفة وضياء المحبة

SULAMI:v1p411#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p411#4/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p411#4/r1.claim: The lasting good deeds are sincere acts and intentions; anything done for God's sake is sincerity.
SULAMI:v1p411#4/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء في قوله : الباقيات الصالحات . قال : هي الأعمال الخالصة والنيات الصادقة

SULAMI:v1p411#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p411#4/r2.speaker: جعفر الصادق
SULAMI:v1p411#4/r2.claim: The lasting good deeds are divine unity, which remains as long as the monotheist remains.
SULAMI:v1p411#4/r2.anchor: قال جعفر الصادق : الباقيات الصالحات هو التوحيد فإنه باق بقاء الموحد

SULAMI:v1p411#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p411#4/r3.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
SULAMI:v1p411#4/r3.claim: The lasting good deeds are sincere counsel to people.
SULAMI:v1p411#4/r3.anchor: وقال يحيى بن معاذ : الباقيات الصالحات هي نصيحة الخلق

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268#4/r1.claim: الباقيات الصالحات is said to mean the five prayers.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268#4/r1.anchor: يقال: الصلوات الخمس. ويقال: سبحان الله

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268#4/r2.claim: Another view glosses الباقيات الصالحات as the phrases “Glory be to God,” “Praise be to God,” and the other statements of remembrance listed.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268#4/r2.anchor: ويقال: سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268#4/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268#4/r3.claim: خير أملا means the best thing you can hope for.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268#4/r3.anchor: وخير أملا} أي خير ما تؤملون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p332/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p332/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p332/r1.claim: This is an admonition to believers: the wealth and children of polytheists are only temporary worldly adornment, while what God prepared for believers is better in reward and hope; see the warning about unbelievers' brief enjoyment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p332/r1.anchor: اعتراض أريد به الموعظة والعبرة للمؤمنين بأن ما فيه المشركون من النعمة من مال وبنين ما هو إلا زينة الحياة الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p332/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p332/r2.speaker: طرفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p332/r2.claim: His poem reflects the well-known Arab pride in wealth and children, imagining having abundant property and noble sons.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p332/r2.anchor:
قال طرفة :
فلو شاء ربي كنت قيس بن عاصم
ولو شاء ربي كنت عمرو بن مرثد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p332/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p332/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p332/r3.claim: The abiding righteous things are good deeds with lasting reward, therefore better than transient worldly adornment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p332/r3.anchor: الصالحات } صفتان جرتا على موصوف محذوف ، أي الأعمال الصالحات الباقيات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p332/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p332/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p332/r4.claim: The expected order would be righteous before abiding, since righteous deeds is the familiar expression and permanence follows from goodness; righteous can stand as a noun for good works, as in the Quran and a line by Jarir.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p332/r4.anchor: لأنهما وإن كانا وصفين لموصوف محذوف إلا أن أعرفهما في وصفية ذلك المحذوف هو الصالحات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p332/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p332/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p332/r5.claim: The order is reversed to stress that wealth and children do not last, compressing the omitted statement that they vanish; the wind-scattered plant in 18:45 indicates this by representation, and abiding adds a reinforcing implication.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p332/r5.anchor: فقدم ( الباقيات ) للتنبيه على أن ما ذكر قبله إنما كان مفصولا لأنه ليس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p334/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p334/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p334/r1.claim: The mountain scene recalls the resurrection after the transient worldly-life parable; it contrasts with the enduring good deeds of 18:46.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p334/r1.anchor: فبعد أن بين لهم تعرض ما هم فيه من نعيم إلى الزوال على وجه الموعظة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r1.claim: Wealth and children answer the pagans’ pride: they adorn worldly life but do not benefit people in the Hereafter.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r1.anchor: هذا رد على المشركين الذين كانوا يفتخرون بالأموال والأولاد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r2.claim: One view identifies lasting good deeds as saying Subḥān Allah, al-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illa Allah, and Allahu akbar; Abu Hurayra transmits a Prophetic report urging these words when night worship or fighting is beyond one’s ability.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r2.anchor: روى أبو هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال إن عجزتم عن الليل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r3.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r3.claim: ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan gives the same formula and adds lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-llāh; Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib and Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi agree.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r3.anchor: وسئل عثمان ابن عفان رضي الله عنه عن الباقيات الصالحات فقال هذه الكلمات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r4.claim: A report from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib from the Prophet gives the formula as lā ilāha illa Allah, Allahu akbar, al-ḥamdu lillāh, and lā quwwata illa bi-llāh.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r4.anchor: أنها لا إله إلا الله والله اكبر والحمد لله ولا قوة الا بالله رواه علي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r5.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr transmits from Ibn ʿAbbas that the lasting good deeds are the five prayers; Ibn Masʿud, Masruq, and Ibrahim share this view.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r5.anchor: أنها الصلوات الخمس رواه سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r6.speaker: العوفي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r6.claim: Al-ʿAwfi transmits from Ibn ʿAbbas that the lasting good deeds are good words.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r6.anchor: الكلام الطيب رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r7.speaker: ابن أبي طلحة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r7.claim: Ibn Abi Talha transmits from Ibn ʿAbbas that the term covers all good deeds; Qatada and Ibn Zayd agree.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r7.anchor: هي جميع أعمال الحسنات وراه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r8.claim: They are better in reward and a better hope than worldly expectations, which may fail, whereas this hope does not.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p149/r8.anchor: لأن آمالكم كواذب وهذا أمل لا يكذب

JISHUMI:v6p4427/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4427/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4427/r1.claim: Righteous deeds are best for the accountable because God commands them, promises reward for them, and threatens punishment for their omission.
JISHUMI:v6p4427/r1.anchor: لأنها أصلح الأعمال للمكلف من حيث أمر بها ووعد الثواب عليها

JISHUMI:v6p4427/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4427/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4427/r2.claim: “Better reward” means the best recompense for an act, and “better hope” means the best object one may hope for; false hopes lead to ruin.
JISHUMI:v6p4427/r2.anchor: خير جزاء على العمل وخير أملا أي: خير شيء يأمله المرء

JISHUMI:v6p4427/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4427/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4427/r3.claim: The verse urges seeking Paradise and detachment from the world by recalling its swift passing and short duration.
JISHUMI:v6p4427/r3.anchor: الحث على طلب الجنة ونعيمها، والزهد في الدنيا من حيث نبه على سرعة فنائها

JISHUMI:v6p4427/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4427/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4427/r4.claim: The world is compared either to water, which does not settle or remain unchanged and may help or harm, or to a briefly beautiful plant that dries, yellows, crumbles, and vanishes in the wind.
JISHUMI:v6p4427/r4.anchor: شبه بالماء من حيث لا يستقر في موضع ولا يبقى على حاله

JISHUMI:v6p4427/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4427/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4427/r5.claim: The imagined question asks why people were not given enough to worship without needing to earn; the answer is that livelihood is a trial, examination, and kindness that prompts reflection.
JISHUMI:v6p4427/r5.anchor: فجوابنا: ابتلاء وامتحانا ولطفا لهم، ليتدبروا

JISHUMI:v6p4427/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4427/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4427/r6.claim: Earning is itself a kind of worship; it humbles people, and their mutual need teaches them that God alone is self-sufficient.
JISHUMI:v6p4427/r6.anchor: ولأن الكسب نوع عبادة، ولأنه تصغير أحواله لعلمه أنه تعالى قادر حي

NASAFI-FULL:v3p16#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p16#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p16#2/r1.claim: Wealth and children adorn worldly life but do not provide provisions for the grave or the afterlife.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p16#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ المال والبنون زينة الحياة الدنيا ﴾ لا زاد القبر وعدة العقبي

NASAFI-FULL:v3p16#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p16#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p16#2/r2.claim: The enduring good works may be any good deed whose fruit remains for a person.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p16#2/r2.anchor: أعمال الخير التي تبقى ثمرتها للانسان

NASAFI-FULL:v3p16#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p16#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p16#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the enduring deeds are the five prayers.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p16#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p16#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p16#2/r4.claim: A further interpretation lists glorifying God, praising Him, declaring His oneness, and magnifying Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p16#2/r4.anchor: أو سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p16#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p16#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p16#2/r5.claim: These works are better in reward and hope because God's promise is true whereas most worldly hopes are false; a person hopes for God's reward here and receives it in the next life.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p16#2/r5.anchor: لأنه وعد صادق وأكثر الآمال كاذبة يعني أن صاحبها يأمل في الدنيا ثواب الله ويصيبه في الآخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r1.claim: Both the singular predicate زينة and dual زينتا are grammatically permitted with the coordinated dual subject.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r1.anchor: ويجوز «زينتا» وهو خبر الابتداء في التثنية والإفراد

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r2.claim: Wealth beautifies and benefits, while children bring strength and defense; together they adorn worldly life, whose fleeting character should deter attachment.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r2.anchor: لأن في المال جمالا ونفعا، وفي البنين قوة ودفعا،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r3.claim: The verse rebukes ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn and others who boasted of wealth and nobility: worldly ornaments are passing delusion, while only provisions for the grave and afterlife endure.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r3.anchor: وهو رد على عيينة بن حصن وأمثاله لما افتخروا بالغنى والشرف

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r4.claim: A saying warns against attaching the heart to wealth, women, or authority because each passes from one possessor to another.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r4.anchor: لا تعقد قلبك مع المال لأنه فيء ذاهب

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r5.claim: Wealth and children are a trial, and spouses or children may become enemies, supporting caution about worldly attachment.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r6.claim: The enduring righteous deeds include obedience performed by Salman, Suhayb, and poor Muslims; they bring better reward and hope than wealth and children without righteous action.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r6.anchor: أي ما يأتي به سلمان وصهيب وفقراء المسلمين من الطاعات

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r7.claim: Calling the deeds better does not praise worldly ornament; the comparison is rhetorical, as in the description of Paradise as a better resting place.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r7.anchor: وليس في زينة الدنيا خير، ولكنه خرج مخرج قوله

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r8.claim: Some say these deeds are truly better than what ignorant people merely suppose to be good.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r8.anchor: وقيل: خير في التحقيق مما يظنه الجهال أنه خير في ظنهم

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r9.claim: The enduring righteous deeds are the five daily prayers; Ibn Jubayr, Abu Maysara, and ʿAmr ibn Shurahbil hold the same view.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r10.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas defines them as every good deed, spoken or performed, that remains for the afterlife; Ibn Zayd agrees.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r10.anchor: أنها كل عمل صالح من قول أو فعل يبقى للآخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r11.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r11.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the broad definition of every enduring good deed, which al-Qurtubi also calls correct because any deed whose reward remains qualifies.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r11.anchor: ورجحه الطبري. وهو الصحيح إن شاء الله لأن كل ما بقي ثوابه جاز أن يقال له هذا

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r12.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r12.claim: Ali distinguishes two harvests: worldly wealth and children, and the afterlife's enduring good deeds; God may grant both to some people.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r12.anchor: الحرث حرثان فحرث الدنيا المال والبنون وحرث الآخرة الباقيات الصالحات

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r13.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r13.claim: The majority identify the deeds as the transmitted glorifications and praises: subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illā Allāh, Allāhu akbar, and lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-llāh.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r13.anchor: وقال الجمهور: هي الكلمات المأثور فضلها

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r14.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r14.claim: Through Malik, ʿUmāra ibn Ṣayyād reports Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab defining them as the formulas of magnification, praise, testimony, and seeking God's aid.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46/r14.anchor: إنها قول العبد الله أكبر وسبحان الله والحمد لله

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r1.claim: A report urges abundant remembrance among the enduring deeds and identifies them as magnification, declaration of divine oneness, glorification, praise, and seeking God's aid; ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq graded it sound.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r2.claim: Qatada transmits a report in which the Prophet likens these formulas to leaves falling from a branch, saying they shed a Muslim's sins and are treasures of Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r2.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أخذ غصنا فخرطه حتى سقط ورقه

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r3.claim: Ibn Mājah gives a similar report from Abū al-Dardāʾ: the four remembrances shed sins like a tree sheds leaves.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r3.anchor: وخرجه ابن ماجه بمعناه من حديث أبي الدرداء قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r4.speaker: الترمذي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r4.claim: Al-Tirmidhi's report from al-Aʿmash, from Anas, compares a dried tree shedding leaves to the shedding of a servant's sins through praise and remembrance; he calls it gharīb and notes al-Aʿmash did not hear from Anas, though he saw him.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r4.anchor: قال: هذا حديث غريب ولا نعرف للأعمش سماعا من أنس

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r5.speaker: الترمذي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports the Prophet met Abraham on the Night Journey, who sent greetings and described Paradise's good soil, sweet water, and barren ground planted by remembrance; al-Tirmidhi calls it ḥasan gharīb.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r6.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r6.claim: Al-Māwardī transmits the same Paradise planting report, adding that lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-llāh is its planting.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r6.anchor: وفيه فقلت: وما غراس الجنة؟ قال: " لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله "

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r7.claim: Ibn Mājah reports that the Prophet told Abū Hurayra that each of the four remembrances he was planting would plant a tree for him in Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#2/r7.anchor: يا أبا هريرة ما الذي تغرس قلت غراسا

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#3/r1.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#3/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the enduring deeds are intentions and aspirations, since deeds are accepted and raised through them.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#3/r1.anchor: هي النيات والهمات لأن بها تقبل الأعمال وترفع

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#3/r2.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#3/r2.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr identifies the deeds as righteous daughters, reading the contrast between worldly sons and what remains as a promise of reward and hope for fathers who treat daughters well.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#3/r2.anchor: هن البنات يدل عليه أوائل الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#3/r3.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#3/r3.claim: Aisha's report about a poor woman and her daughters is cited as evidence for the interpretation of enduring deeds as righteous daughters, with its earlier discussion located in al-Naḥl.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#3/r3.anchor: وقد ذكرناه في سورة النحل في قوله

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#3/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#3/r4.claim: A report describes a man from the Muslim community being led toward Hell, when his daughters plead that he treated them well; God then shows him mercy.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#3/r4.anchor: لقد رأيت رجلا من أمتي أمر به إلى النار

QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#3/r5.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#3/r5.claim: Qatada says the child promised to Moses' parents in 18:81 was a daughter; she married a prophet and bore twelve sons, all prophets.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:46#3/r5.anchor: أبدلهما منه ابنة فتزوجها نبي فولدت له اثني عشر غلاما كلهم أنبياء

SAMIN-DURR:18:46/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:46/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:46/r1.claim: زينة is singular although predicated of wealth and sons because it is a verbal noun: they are themselves adornment by emphasis or things that adorn.
SAMIN-DURR:18:46/r1.anchor: إنما أفرد " زينة " وإن كانت خبرا عن بنين لأنها مصدر، فالتقدير: ذوا زينة

SAMIN-DURR:18:46/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:46/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:46/r2.claim: A rare reading has the dual زينتا الحياة; the alif is not pronounced before the following consonant cluster, which can make it look like the accusative singular.
SAMIN-DURR:18:46/r2.anchor: وقرئ شاذا " زينتا الحياة " على التثنية، وسقطت ألفها لفظا لالتقاء الساكنين

RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r1.claim: Wealth and children are transient adornments, so it is irrational to boast, rejoice, or assign them lasting worth; this rebuts wealthy polytheists’ taunts against poor believers.
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r1.anchor: فهذا برهان باهر على فساد قول أولئك المشركين الذين افتخروا على فقراء المؤمنين بكثرة الأموال والأولاد

RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r2.claim: Lasting afterlife goods are better than perishing worldly goods; intellectual and spiritual goods outrank sensory ones, especially because the afterlife unites both kinds of happiness.
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r2.anchor: وخيرات الآخرة دائمة باقية والدائم الباقي خير من المنقرض المنقضي

RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r3.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r3.claim: One view identifies the lasting good works as the four glorifications: Subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illā Allāh, and Allāhu akbar.
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r3.anchor: قيل إنها قولنا : ( سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر )

RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r4.speaker: الشيخ الغزالي
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r4.claim: Al-Ghazali explains the fourfold reward as ascending knowledge: declaring God free of defect, recognizing Him as source of good, affirming His oneness, and acknowledging that His greatness exceeds reason’s grasp.
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r4.anchor: وللشيخ الغزالي رحمه الله في تفسير هذه الكلمات وجه لطيف

RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r5.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r5.claim: A second reported interpretation identifies the lasting good works as the five daily prayers.
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r5.anchor: والقول الثاني : أن الباقيات الصالحات هي الصلوات الخمس

RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r6.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r6.claim: A third interpretation takes them as good speech, as in the description of the people of Paradise.
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r6.anchor: والقول الثالث : أنها الطيب من القول كما قال تعالى : { وهدوا إلى الطيب من القول }

RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r7.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r7.claim: A fourth view includes every deed or utterance that directs a person to know, love, and serve God; attention to all else is futile because it perishes.
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r7.anchor: أن كل عمل وقول دعاك إلى الاشتغال بمعرفة الله وبمحبته وخدمته فهو الباقيات الصالحات

RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r8.claim: Anything done for God yields better reward and hope, since its doer hopes for God’s reward in this life and a share in the next.
RAZI-FULL:v21p111#2/r8.anchor: أي كل عمل أريد به وجه الله فلا شك أن ما يتعلق به من الثواب وما يتعلق به من الأمل يكون خيرا

STUDYQURAN:18:46/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:46/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:46/r1.claim: Wealth and children adorn worldly life as sources of status and security, but do not necessarily indicate divine favor, protect from punishment, or endure.
STUDYQURAN:18:46/r1.anchor: Wealth and children are the adornment of this world, because they are considered a source of status and security

STUDYQURAN:18:46/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:46/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:46/r2.claim: Righteous deeds endure because they bring lasting reward in the Hereafter, as also stated in 19:76.
STUDYQURAN:18:46/r2.anchor: righteous deeds “endure” in that they bring lasting reward in the Hereafter

TAB-FULL:v15p273/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p273/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p273/r1.claim: Money and children are worldly adornment, exemplified by Uyayna and al-Aqra boasting over Salman, Khabbab, and Suhayb; the latter’s worship and sincere prayer endure and exceed worldly wealth in reward and hope.
TAB-FULL:v15p273/r1.anchor: وما يعمل سلمان وخباب وصهيب من طاعة الله، ودعائهم ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه

TAB-FULL:v15p273/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p273/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p273/r2.claim: The passage from the command to recite revelation through this verse is said to have been revealed about Uyayna and al-Aqra.
TAB-FULL:v15p273/r2.anchor: وهذه الآيات من لدن قوله: {واتل ما أوحي إليك من كتاب ربك} [الكهف: 27] إلى هذا الموضع، ذكر أنها نزلت في عيينة والأقرع

TAB-FULL:v15p273/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p273/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v15p273/r3.claim: Al-Suddi transmits Khabbab’s account of the incident about Uyayna and al-Aqra that begins with the command not to drive away those who call upon God at morning and evening.
TAB-FULL:v15p273/r3.anchor: عن السدي، عن أبي سعيد الأزدي، وكان قارئ الأزد، عن أبي الكنود، عن خباب، في قوله: {ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي} [الأنعام: 52]

TAB-FULL:v15p273/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p273/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p273/r4.claim: Reported interpretations of the enduring good deeds include the five prayers, remembrance of God, all obedience to God, or good speech.
TAB-FULL:v15p273/r4.anchor: فقال بعضهم: هي الصلوات الخمس. وقال بعضهم: هي ذكر الله بالتسبيح والتقديس والتهليل، ونحو ذلك،

TAB-FULL:v15p273/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p273/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p273/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the enduring good deeds as the five daily prayers.
TAB-FULL:v15p273/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، أنه قال: الباقيات الصالحات: الصلوات الخمس

TAB-FULL:v15p275/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p275/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v15p275/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr interprets the enduring good deeds as the five prayers.
TAB-FULL:v15p275/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، في قوله: {والباقيات الصالحات} [الكهف: 46] قال: الصلوات الخمس

TAB-FULL:v15p275/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p275/r2.speaker: عمرو بن شرحبيل
TAB-FULL:v15p275/r2.claim: Amr ibn Shurahbil says the phrase refers to the prescribed prayers.
TAB-FULL:v15p275/r2.anchor: عن عمرو بن شرحبيل، في هذه الآية {والباقيات الصالحات} [الكهف: 46] قال: هي الصلوات المكتوبات

TAB-FULL:v15p275/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p275/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p275/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the enduring good deeds as the five prayers.
TAB-FULL:v15p275/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: {الباقيات الصالحات} [الكهف: 46] : الصلوات الخمس

TAB-FULL:v15p275/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p275/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v15p275/r4.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi likewise says they are the five prayers.
TAB-FULL:v15p275/r4.anchor: عن إبراهيم، قال {الباقيات الصالحات} [الكهف: 46] الصلوات الخمس

TAB-FULL:v15p275/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p275/r5.speaker: أبو ميسرة
TAB-FULL:v15p275/r5.claim: Abu Maysara also interprets them as the five prayers.
TAB-FULL:v15p275/r5.anchor: عن أبي ميسرة، {والباقيات الصالحات} [الكهف: 46] قال: الصلوات الخمس

TAB-FULL:v15p275/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p275/r6.speaker: عثمان
TAB-FULL:v15p275/r6.claim: Uthman interprets the enduring good deeds as the declarations of divine oneness, glorification, praise, magnification, and dependence on God.
TAB-FULL:v15p275/r6.anchor: قيل لعثمان: ما {الباقيات الصالحات} [الكهف: 46] ؟ قال: هن لا إله إلا الله، وسبحان الله، والحمد لله، والله أكبر،

TAB-FULL:v15p278/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p278/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p278/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas gives the four central remembrances: glorification, praise, divine oneness, and magnification.
TAB-FULL:v15p278/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {والباقيات الصالحات} [الكهف: 46] قال: سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر

TAB-FULL:v15p278/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p278/r2.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
TAB-FULL:v15p278/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib includes the four remembrances and the declaration that there is no power or strength except through God.
TAB-FULL:v15p278/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب، قال: {الباقيات الصالحات} [الكهف: 46] سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر، ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله

TAB-FULL:v15p278/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p278/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v15p278/r3.claim: Ibn Umar includes the four remembrances and the declaration that there is no power or strength except through God; Ata ibn Abi Rabah is said to agree.
TAB-FULL:v15p278/r3.anchor: سأل ابن عمر عن {الباقيات الصالحات} [الكهف: 46] ، قال: لا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر، وسبحان الله، ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله

TAB-FULL:v15p278/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p278/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p278/r4.claim: Mujahid lists the four remembrances as the enduring good deeds.
TAB-FULL:v15p278/r4.anchor: عن منصور، عن مجاهد، قال: {الباقيات الصالحات} [الكهف: 46] : سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر

TAB-FULL:v15p278/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p278/r5.speaker: أبو أيوب الأنصاري
TAB-FULL:v15p278/r5.claim: Abu Ayyub transmits a Prophetic account in which Abraham identifies la hawla wa-la quwwata illa bi-llah as planting in Paradise, whose soil is good and spacious.
TAB-FULL:v15p278/r5.anchor: فإن أبا أيوب الأنصاري حدثني أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يقول: " عرج بي إلى السماء فأريت إبراهيم،

TAB-FULL:v15p280/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p280/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v15p280/r1.claim: A Prophetic report from Abu Hurayra names the four remembrances—glorification, praise, divine oneness, and magnification—as among the enduring good deeds.
TAB-FULL:v15p280/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر من الباقيات الصالحات

TAB-FULL:v15p280/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p280/r2.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p280/r2.claim: Hasan and Qatada identify the enduring good deeds with the four remembrances: divine oneness, magnification, praise, and glorification.
TAB-FULL:v15p280/r2.anchor: عن الحسن، وقتادة، في قوله: {والباقيات الصالحات خير} [الكهف: 46] قال: لا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر، والحمد لله، وسبحان الله، هن الباقيات الصالحات

TAB-FULL:v15p280/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p280/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
TAB-FULL:v15p280/r3.claim: The Prophet urges abundant enduring good deeds, explaining that they are the religion and listing magnification, divine oneness, glorification, praise, and la hawla wa-la quwwata illa bi-llah.
TAB-FULL:v15p280/r3.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «استكثروا من الباقيات الصالحات» ، قيل: وما هي يا رسول الله؟ قال: «الملة»

TAB-FULL:v15p280/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p280/r4.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
TAB-FULL:v15p280/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib rejects prayer and fasting, then almsgiving and pilgrimage, as the specific referent and identifies five devotional phrases instead.
TAB-FULL:v15p280/r4.anchor: سألني سعيد بن المسيب، عن الباقيات الصالحات، فقلت: الصلاة والصيام، قال: لم تصب، فقلت: الزكاة والحج، فقال: لم تصب

TAB-FULL:v15p280#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p280#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p280#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the enduring good deeds include remembrance and all good works, from prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, charity, freeing slaves, jihad, and kinship to other acts of goodness.
TAB-FULL:v15p280#2/r1.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {والباقيات الصالحات} [الكهف: 46] قال: هي ذكر الله، قول لا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر،

TAB-FULL:v15p280#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p280#2/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p280#2/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd simply identifies them as righteous deeds.
TAB-FULL:v15p280#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله {والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثوابا وخير أملا} [الكهف: 46] قال: الأعمال الصالحة

TAB-FULL:v15p280#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p280#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p280#2/r3.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas identifies them as good words.
TAB-FULL:v15p280#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {والباقيات الصالحات} [الكهف: 46] قال: الكلام الطيب

TAB-FULL:v15p280#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p280#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p280#2/r4.claim: Al-Tabari prefers all good works as the referent, since every righteous act remains for its doer and earns reward; neither Scripture nor a Prophetic report restricts the phrase to a subset.
TAB-FULL:v15p280#2/r4.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب، قول من قال: هن جميع أعمال الخير، كالذي روي عن علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس،

TAB-FULL:v15p280#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p280#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p280#2/r5.claim: The report naming four remembrances says they are among the enduring good deeds, not that they exhaust the category, so other righteous works also qualify.
TAB-FULL:v15p280#2/r5.anchor: ولم يقل: هن جميع الباقيات الصالحات، ولا كل الباقيات الصالحات، وجائز أن تكون هذه باقيات صالحات، وغيرها من أعمال البر أيضا باقيات صالحات

ZAJJAJ:v3p292/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p292/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ZAJJAJ:v3p292/r1.claim: Some identify the enduring good deeds as the five daily prayers; others identify them as the four phrases of glorification, praise, monotheism, and magnification.
ZAJJAJ:v3p292/r1.anchor:
(الباقيات الصالحات) هي الصلوات الخمس، - وقيل هي: سبحان الله
والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر.

ZAJJAJ:v3p292/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p292/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p292/r2.claim: More broadly, they are every righteous deed whose reward remains, including prayer, monotheism, praise, charity, fasting, jihad, and all good works.
ZAJJAJ:v3p292/r2.anchor:
والباقيات الصالحات - والله أعلم -
كل عمل صالح يبقى ثوابه، فالصلوات الخمس وتوحيد الله وتعظيمه داخل

ASAD-NOTES:18:45#n49/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:45#n49/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:45#n49/r1.claim: Baqiyat as-salihat means good deeds whose fruit endures forever, and the expression also occurs at 19:76.
ASAD-NOTES:18:45#n49/r1.anchor: ("good deeds, the fruit whereof endures forever") occurs in the Qur'an twice - in the above verse as well as in 19:76

ASAD-NOTES:18:45#n49/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:45#n49/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:45#n49/r2.claim: The phrase literally compares these deeds as better in God’s sight for merit and for hope.
ASAD-NOTES:18:45#n49/r2.anchor: "are better in thy Sustainer's sight - as regards merit, and better as regards hope"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r1.claim: This rebukes ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn, al-Aqraʿ, and leaders proud of wealth and children: these adorn worldly life but do not benefit in the Hereafter; the enduring good deeds contrast with what Salman and Suhayb do.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r1.anchor: هذا رد على عيينة بن حصين، والأقرع والرؤساء الذين كانوا يفتخرون بالمال والغنى والأبناء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية سعيد بن جبير؛ مسروق؛ إبراهيم؛ محمد بن كعب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r2.claim: One interpretation of the enduring good deeds is the five daily prayers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء؛ مجاهد؛ عكرمة؛ الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r3.claim: Another interpretation is the glorifications: subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illā Allāh, and Allāhu akbar.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r3.anchor: يريد سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r4.speaker: أنس؛ أبو هريرة؛ الخدري؛ عثمان؛ ابن عمر؛ سعيد بن المسيب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r4.claim: A Prophetic report names those remembrances the enduring good deeds; another group adds lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-llāh.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r4.anchor: أن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- سمى هذه الأذكار الباقيات الصالحات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية العوفي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r5.claim: The phrase can mean good speech, which is also a form of remembrance of God.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية الوالبي؛ قتادة؛ الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r6.claim: It can mean righteous deeds and all good actions done for God; al-Zajjāj chooses every righteous deed whose reward remains.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p35#3/r6.anchor: هي كل عمل صالح يبقى ثوابه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p37/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p37/r1.speaker: ابن عباس؛ الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p37/r1.claim: The enduring deeds are better in reward and hope than wealth and children; Arabic uses “better” even where the comparison offers nothing good, and hope in good work surpasses hope in evil work.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p37/r1.anchor: يريد أفضل ثوابا وأفضل أملا من المال والبنين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p37/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p37/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p37/r2.claim: Better hope means better than what people hope to obtain from wealth and children.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p37/r2.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: ({وخير أملا} مما يؤملون)

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p189/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p189/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p189/r1.claim: The lasting good things are better in outcome and are the best reward servants can hope to receive in the Hereafter.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p410#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p410#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p410#2/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the lasting good deeds as declaring God’s oneness and saying ‘Glory be to God,’ ‘Praise be to God,’ and ‘God is greatest.’
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p410#2/r1.anchor: عن منصور عن مجاهد قال ﴿ والباقيات الصالحات ﴾ لا إله إلا الله وسبحان الله والحمد لله والله أكبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p185/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p185/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p185/r3.claim: Money and children are transient ornaments, so believers should not be impressed by ʿUyayna and his peers boasting of wealth and offspring.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p185/r3.anchor: ما افتخر به عيينة وأضرابه من المال والبنين إنما ذلك زينة هذه الحياة الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p185/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p185/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p185/r4.claim: Zīna may imply an omitted possessor or treat money and children as abundance; either way, worldly ornaments perish and boasting is foolish.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p185/r4.anchor: على تقدير حذف مضاف أي مقر زينة أو وضع المال والبنين منزلة المعنى والكثرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p185/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p185/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p185/r5.claim: This reasoning refutes polytheists who boasted to poor believers about wealth and children.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p185/r5.anchor: فساد قول أولئك المشركين الذين افتخروا على فقراء المؤمنين بكثرة الأموال والأولاد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p185/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p185/r6.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p185/r6.claim: The majority identify enduring good deeds with the famous phrases of glorification, praise, divine unity, greatness, and reliance on God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p185/r6.anchor: قال الجمهور هي الكلمات المأثور فضلها سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله

ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r1.claim: Wealth and sons are the worldly adornments about which the unbelieving brother boasted; wealth precedes sons because it is more fundamentally tied to adornment and support.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r1.anchor: بيان لشأن ما كانوا يفتخرون به من محسنات الحياة الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r2.claim: Wealth adorns and supports parents and children alike at all times, while sons adorn and support only those who become parents; wealth sustains individual life, sons the species, and wealth is more urgently needed and comes first.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r2.anchor: وعمومه بالنسبة إلى الإفراد والأوقات فإنه زينة وممد لكل أحد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r3.claim: Wealth can be an adornment without sons, but sons without wealth leave a person in distress; ornament is a verbal noun transferred to the thing used for adornment for emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r3.anchor: ولأنه زينة بدونهم من غير عكس فإن من له بنون بلا مال

ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r4.claim: The genitive ties these ornaments specifically to worldly life; alternatively it means ornaments found in worldly life, whose rapid decay makes their ornaments perish even sooner.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r4.anchor: وجوز أن تكون على معنى في والمعنى أن ما يفتخرون به

ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r5.claim: The verse's implicit argument is that worldly life quickly vanishes, so its ornaments do too, and a wise person should not boast of things that vanish quickly.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r5.anchor: وكل ما كان سريع الزوال يقبح بالعاقل أن يفتخر به

ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r6.speaker: رسول الله
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r6.claim: The Prophet urges believers to increase the enduring good deeds, naming takbir, tahlil, tasbih, tahmid, and saying there is no power or strength except through God; reported from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r6.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال استكثروا من الباقيات الصالحات

ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r7.speaker: رسول الله
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r7.claim: The Prophet identifies the enduring deeds as glorifying, praising, affirming God's oneness, magnifying God, and declaring there is no power or strength except through God; they erase sins like a tree sheds leaves and are Paradise's treasures, in a report from Abu al-Darda.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p286/r7.anchor: سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله

ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r1.claim: A second report from Ibn Abbas identifies the enduring deeds with the five daily prayers.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r1.anchor: في رواية أخرى عنه تفسيرها بالصلوات الخمس وأخرج ابن مردويه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r2.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas interprets them as all good deeds.
