ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r2.anchor: في رواية أخرى عنه أيضا تفسيرها بجميع أعمال الحسنات وفي معناه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r3.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r3.claim: Qatada says the enduring deeds are everything done seeking God's approval.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r3.anchor: عن قتادة أنها كل ما أريد به وجه الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r4.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r4.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the enduring deeds as good intentions.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r4.anchor: عن الحسن وابن عطاء أنها النيات الصالحة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r5.speaker: ابن عطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r5.claim: Ibn Ata also interprets the enduring deeds as good intentions.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r5.anchor: عن الحسن وابن عطاء أنها النيات الصالحة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r6.speaker: الطبري
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r6.claim: Al-Tabari and others select Ibn Abbas's report that the phrase covers all good deeds, a general meaning that includes the specific interpretations in the reports.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r6.anchor: واختار الطبري وغيره ما في الرواية الأخيرة عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r7.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r7.claim: Al-Khafaji argues that narrower explanations are examples of the general category; al-Alusi questions this because the Prophet's wording these are implies restriction after naming specific acts.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r7.anchor: وادعى الخفاجي أن كل ما ذكر في تفسيرها غير العام ذكر على طريق التمثيل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r8.claim: Enduring is an adjective of omitted words or deeds, and their reward is what endures; alternatively the adjective is attached by ellipsis to a deleted noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r8.anchor: فالباقيات صفة لمقدر كالكلمات أو الأعمال وإسناد الباقيات إلى ذلك مجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r9.claim: Poor believers who call on God morning and evening seeking His face are included first of all; the passage honors them and lowers the status of their detractors.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r9.anchor: وكذا تدخل أعمال فقراء المؤمنين الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r10.claim: These deeds are better with God in the afterlife, where their excellence appears; alternatively with God means according to His judgment, and the comparison is not that deeds outrank wealth in their shared worldly basis.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r10.anchor: أي في الآخرة وهو بيان لما يظهر فيه آثار خيريتها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r11.claim: Thawaban means reward and recompense, or alternatively benefit.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r12.claim: The good deeds are better hope because they realize in the afterlife what their doer hopes for, whereas wealth and sons do not; repeating better emphasizes the point or signals distinct grounds of superiority.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p287/r12.anchor: حيث ينال بها صاحبها في الآخرة ما يؤمله بها في الدنيا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ikrima, and Mujahid identify the enduring good deeds as saying the four phrases of glorification, praise, monotheism, and magnification.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r1.anchor: ابن عباس وعكرمة ومجاهد: هي قول سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r2.claim: A Prophetic report calls these four phrases the best words.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r2.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "أفضل الكلام أربع كلمات: سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits that saying the four phrases is dearer to the Prophet than everything on which the sun rises.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لأن أقول سبحان الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r4.claim: Abu Said transmits an instruction to increase the enduring good deeds, identified as magnification, tahlil, glorification, praise, and the declaration of God's power; no grading is stated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "استكثروا من الباقيات الصالحات"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r5.claim: Said ibn Jubayr, Masruq, and Ibrahim identify the enduring good deeds as the five prayers; another report attributes this view to Ibn Abbas.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r5.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير ومسروق وإبراهيم: "الباقيات الصالحات" هي: الصلوات الخمس.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r6.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas identifies the enduring good deeds as righteous actions, also the view of Qatada.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p174#2/r6.anchor:
ابن عباس (4) .
وعنه رواية أخرى: أنها الأعمال الصالحة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p175/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p175/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p175/r1.claim: Better reward means better recompense from God; better hope means what a person hopes for.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p175/r1.anchor: {خير عند ربك ثوابا} أي جزاء المراد {وخير أملا} أي ما يأمله الإنسان.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:46/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:46/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:46/r1.claim: Wealth and children adorn earthly life but soon perish; enduring good works retain fruit forever and include prayers, pilgrimage, Ramadan fasting, praises of God, and good speech.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:46/r1.anchor: وأعمال الخيرات التي تبقى له ثمرتها أبد الآباد، ويندرج فيها ما فسرت به

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:46/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:46/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:46/r2.claim: Good works are better in reward and hope because they bring in the afterlife what people hoped to gain through worldly things.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:46/r2.anchor: خير عند ربك } من المال والبنين. { ثوابا } عائدة. { وخير أملا } لأن صاحبها ينال بها في الآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p472/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p472/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p472/r1.claim: The lasting good deeds surpass transient wealth and children in this life and the next; their reward remains and prospects rise, while worldly possessions fail when most needed.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p472/r1.anchor: خير من المال والبنين في العاجل والآجل

BIQAI-FULL:v4p472/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p472/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p472/r2.claim: The reward is better with the Lord, who knows outcomes, and the hope associated with it is better than hope invested in money and children.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p472/r2.anchor: لأن ثوابها إلى بقاء , وأملها كل ساعة في تحقيق

DURR-FULL:v5p396/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r1.speaker: غير مسمى
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r1.claim: An unidentified speaker says a child who was worldly adornment yesterday is today among the enduring good deeds, as the speaker counts the loss as a spiritual reward.
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r1.anchor: فقال: وما يمنعني أن أحتسبه وكان أمس من زينة الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v5p396/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r2.claim: Wealth and children are the harvest of worldly life, while righteous action is the harvest of the afterlife; God may grant both to some people.
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r2.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: {المال والبنون} حرث الدنيا والعمل الصالح حرث الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v5p396/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r3.claim: The enduring good deeds are saying ‘glory be to God,’ ‘praise be to God,’ ‘there is no god but God,’ and ‘God is greatest.’
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {والباقيات الصالحات} قال سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله

DURR-FULL:v5p396/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r4.claim: The Prophet urges abundant recitation of the enduring good deeds, identifying them as takbir, tahlil, tasbih, tahmid, and ‘there is no power or strength except through God.’
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r4.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: استكثروا من الباقيات الصالحات

DURR-FULL:v5p396/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r5.claim: The Prophet calls tasbih, tahmid, tahlil, and takbir among the enduring good deeds.
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r5.anchor: عن النعمان بن بشير: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ألا وأن سبحان الله

DURR-FULL:v5p396/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r6.claim: The Prophet calls the four phrases a shield from Hell that will come on Judgment Day as deeds preceding and following their speaker and commending him.
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: خذوا جنتكم قيل: يا رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v5p396/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r7.claim: The Prophet says five remembrance phrases erase sins like leaves falling from a tree and are treasures of Paradise and enduring good deeds.
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r7.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله

DURR-FULL:v5p396/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r8.claim: The Prophet says that reciting the four remembrance phrases causes sins to fall away like leaves from a dry tree, and God calls them enduring good deeds.
DURR-FULL:v5p396/r8.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال: مر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بشجرة يابسة

DURR-FULL:v5p398/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r1.speaker: سعد بن جنادة
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r1.claim: The Prophet taught Sa‘d three short suras and the four remembrance phrases, calling the phrases the enduring good deeds.
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r1.anchor: عن سعد بن جنادة قال: أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأسلمت وعلمني (قل هو الله أحد

DURR-FULL:v5p398/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r2.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r2.claim: ‘Uthman identifies the enduring good deeds as the four remembrance phrases plus ‘there is no power or strength except through God.’
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r2.anchor: عن عثمان بن عفان أنه سئل عن {والباقيات الصالحات} قال: هي لا إله إلا الله

DURR-FULL:v5p398/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r3.claim: Ibn ‘Umar gives the same five remembrance phrases as the enduring good deeds.
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r3.anchor: عن ابن عمر أنه سئل عن {والباقيات الصالحات} قال: لا إله إلا الله والله أكبر

DURR-FULL:v5p398/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r4.claim: The enduring good deeds include many kinds of worship and goodness—remembrance and seeking forgiveness, prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, charity, emancipation, jihad, and kinship—because they remain for their people in Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: {والباقيات الصالحات} قال: هي ذكر الله لا إله إلا الله والله أكبر وسبحان الله

DURR-FULL:v5p398/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r5.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r5.claim: Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas said that in a brief silence he uttered words better than all the water of the Nile and Euphrates: the four phrases of remembrance.
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب قال: كنا عند سعد بن أبي وقاص فسكت سكتة

DURR-FULL:v5p398/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r6.claim: The enduring good deeds are words of goodness.
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس {والباقيات الصالحات} قال: الكلام الطيب

DURR-FULL:v5p398/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r7.claim: Those who remember God with the four phrases are described as circling the Throne with a buzzing sound and being mentioned by God; the report asks whether one would not want to remain remembered by the Merciful.
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r7.anchor: عن النعمان بن بشير قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: الذين يذكرون من جلال الله

DURR-FULL:v5p398/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r8.claim: For someone unable to memorize any Qur’an, the Prophet taught the four remembrance phrases and ‘there is no power or strength except through God’ as a sufficient substitute.
DURR-FULL:v5p398/r8.anchor: عن عبد الله بن أبي أوفى قال: أتى رجل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فذكر أنه لا يستطيع

DURR-FULL:v5p399/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r1.claim: The Prophet says an angel carries the remembrance phrases upward, and every assembly of angels they pass prays for the speaker until they reach God.
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r1.anchor: عن موسى بن طلحة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: كلمات إذا قالهن العبد

DURR-FULL:v5p399/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r2.speaker: الحسن البصري
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r2.claim: In a dream story, people take up weapons at a heavenly warning, but a voice identifies the four remembrance phrases as the true protection against fear.
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r2.anchor: عن الحسن البصري قال: رأى رجل في المنام أن مناديا نادى في السماء

DURR-FULL:v5p399/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r3.claim: The Prophet says that uttering the four remembrance phrases is more beloved than giving that many dinars in charity.
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: لأن أقول سبحان الله

DURR-FULL:v5p399/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r4.claim: ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr says reciting the four remembrance phrases is dearer to him than carrying the same number of bridled horses into battle.
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: لأن أقول سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله

DURR-FULL:v5p399/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r5.claim: A person who says ‘praise be to God,’ ‘God is greatest,’ or ‘there is no god but God’ receives the stated good deeds and erasure of bad deeds for each phrase.
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: من قال من قبل نفسه الحمد لله رب العالمين كتب الله له ثلاثين حسنة

DURR-FULL:v5p399/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r6.claim: The enduring good deeds are the five daily prayers, identified with the statement that good deeds erase bad ones in 11:114.
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال: في قوله: {والباقيات الصالحات} {الحسنات يذهبن السيئات

DURR-FULL:v5p399/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r7.claim: Every act of obedience to God is an enduring good deed.
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r7.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {والباقيات الصالحات} قال: كل شيء من طاعة الله

DURR-FULL:v5p399/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r8.claim: Anything done seeking God’s favor is an enduring good deed.
DURR-FULL:v5p399/r8.anchor: عن قتادة أنه سئل عن {والباقيات الصالحات} فقال: كل ما أريد به وجه الله

DURR-FULL:v5p400/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p400/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p400/r1.claim: The enduring reward with God is better than the reward received by the polytheists.
DURR-FULL:v5p400/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله: {خير عند ربك ثوابا} قال: خير جزاء من جزاء المشركين

DURR-FULL:v5p400/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p400/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p400/r2.claim: Every worker has a hoped-for outcome, and the believer has among the best hopes.
DURR-FULL:v5p400/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {وخير أملا} قال: إن لكل عامل أملا يؤمله وإن المؤمن من خير الناس أملا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r7.claim: Enduring good deeds are lasting love, knowledge, intimacy with God, sincere tawḥīd and turning from others; the phrase may include all sincere deeds and intentions.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r7.anchor: قيل هي المحبة الدائمة والمعرفة الكاملة والأنس بالله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p520/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p520/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير وأبو ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p520/r1.claim: They identify enduring righteous deeds as the five daily prayers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p520/r1.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وابن جبير وأبو ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل: هي الصلوات الخمس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p520/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p520/r2.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p520/r2.claim: The majority identify them as formulas of glorification, praise, unity, greatness, and reliance; reports urge frequent recitation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p520/r2.anchor: وقال الجمهور هي الكلمات المأثور فضلها: سبحان الله والحمد الله ولا إله إلا الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p520/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p520/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p520/r3.claim: Another view defines them as every good word or deed preserved for the afterlife; al-Ṭabarī prefers it and author says Ibn ʿAbbās' views indicate generality.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p520/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا الباقيات الصالحات: كل عمل صالح من قول أو فعل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p520/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p520/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p520/r4.claim: Their doer has better reward and hope than one with wealth and children but no righteous work.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p520/r4.anchor: صاحبها ينتظر الثواب وينبسط على خير من حال ذي المال والبنين

JISHUMI:v6p4428/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4428/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4428/r1.claim: People should focus on the Hereafter and righteous action rather than wealth and children, worldly adornment.
JISHUMI:v6p4428/r1.anchor: الحياة الدنيا، وأن يكون اهتمامه بالآخرة وطلبها بالاعمال الصالحة.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p678/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p678/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p678/r1.claim: The enduring righteous deeds are good acts whose fruits remain for a person while worldly desires and benefits perish.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p678/r1.anchor: أعمال الخير التي تبقى ثمرتها للإنسان وتفنى عنه كل ما تطمح إليه نفسه من حظوظ الدنيا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p678/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p678/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p678/r2.claim: One view identifies the enduring deeds as the five daily prayers.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p678/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p678/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p678/r3.claim: Another view identifies them as saying glorification, praise, that none is god but God, and God is greatest.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p678/r3.anchor: وقيل : سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إلاه إلا الله والله أكبر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p678/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p678/r4.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p678/r4.claim: Qatāda says the phrase includes everything done seeking God’s pleasure.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p678/r4.anchor: وعن قتادة : كل ما أريد به وجه الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p678/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p678/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p678/r5.claim: They are better in reward and hope: their doer hopes for God’s reward in this world and receives it in the next.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p678/r5.anchor: أي ما يتعلق بها من الثواب وما يتعلق بها من الأمل ؛ لأن صاحبها يأمل

TABRISI:18:47/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:47/r12.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
TABRISI:18:47/r12.claim: Bāqiyāt ṣāliḥāt are acts of obedience and all good deeds, whose reward lasts forever.
TABRISI:18:47/r12.anchor: وهي الطاعات لله تعالى وجميع الحسنات لأن ثوابها يبقى أبدا عن ابن عباس وقتادة

TABRISI:18:47#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:47#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:18:47#2/r1.claim: Bāqiyāt ṣāliḥāt may mean the four remembrances recited by poor Muslims such as Salmān and Ṣuhayb.
TABRISI:18:47#2/r1.anchor: إن الباقيات الصالحات هي ما كان يأتي به سلمان وصهيب

TABRISI:18:47#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:47#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
TABRISI:18:47#2/r2.claim: This explanation of the enduring deeds as four remembrances is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās via ʿAṭāʾ and also from Mujāhid and ʿIkrimah.
TABRISI:18:47#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في رواية عطاء ومجاهد وعكرمة

TABRISI:18:47#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:47#2/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TABRISI:18:47#2/r3.claim: The Prophet calls the four remembrances a shield from Hell, describing them as provisions, responses, sequels, and enduring good deeds.
TABRISI:18:47#2/r3.anchor: وروى أنس بن مالك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

TABRISI:18:47#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:47#2/r4.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:18:47#2/r4.claim: The Prophet says those unable to endure night vigil or fight should persist in the four remembrances, which are enduring good deeds.
TABRISI:18:47#2/r4.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

TABRISI:18:47#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:47#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود وسعيد بن جبير ومسروق والنخعي
TABRISI:18:47#2/r5.claim: Bāqiyāt ṣāliḥāt may mean the five daily prayers; this is also reported from Abū ʿAbd Allāh.
TABRISI:18:47#2/r5.anchor: هي الصلوات الخمس عن ابن مسعود وسعيد بن جبير ومسروق والنخعي

TABRISI:18:47#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:47#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:18:47#2/r6.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh is also reported to identify the enduring good deeds as night prayer.
TABRISI:18:47#2/r6.anchor: أن من الباقيات الصالحات القيام باليل لصلاة الليل

TABRISI:18:47#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:47#2/r7.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:18:47#2/r7.claim: Another view identifies enduring good deeds as righteous daughters.
TABRISI:18:47#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: إن الباقيات الصالحات هن البنات الصالحات

TABRISI:18:47#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:47#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:47#2/r8.claim: The author prefers the general sense, encompassing every act of obedience and good deed.
TABRISI:18:47#2/r8.anchor: والأولى حملها على العموم فيدخل فيها جميع الطاعات والخيرات

TABRISI:18:47#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:47#2/r9.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:18:47#2/r9.claim: In Ibn ʿUqda's book, Abū ʿAbd Allāh tells al-Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān not to deem their love small, since it is among the enduring good deeds.
TABRISI:18:47#2/r9.anchor: وفي كتاب ابن عقدة أن أبا عبد الله ع قال للحصين

TABRISI:18:47#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:47#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:47#2/r10.claim: The deeds are called righteous because God commanded them, promised reward, and threatened punishment for leaving them.
TABRISI:18:47#2/r10.anchor: وإنما سميت الطاعات صالحات لأنها أصلح الأعمال للمكلف

THALABI:v6p174/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p174/r1.speaker: أبو أيوب الأنصاري عن النبي
THALABI:v6p174/r1.claim: On the Prophet’s ascent, Abraham asked him to urge his community to plant more in Paradise’s good soil; its planting formula is ‘There is no power or strength except through God.’
THALABI:v6p174/r1.anchor: فأتيت أبا أيوب الأنصاري فحدث أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

THALABI:v6p174/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p174/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وعمرو بن شرحبيل ومسروق وإبراهيم
THALABI:v6p174/r2.claim: They identify lasting good deeds as the five prayers and as good deeds that erase sins.
THALABI:v6p174/r2.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير وعمرو بن شرحبيل ومسروق وإبراهيم: هي الصلوات الخمسة،

THALABI:v6p174/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p174/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p174/r3.claim: He lists lasting deeds as testimony, seeking forgiveness, blessing Muhammad, prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, charity, freeing slaves, jihad, kinship, and every good deed enduring for its owner in Paradise.
THALABI:v6p174/r3.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس: هي الأعمال الصالحة: لا إله إلا الله،

THALABI:v6p174/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p174/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p174/r4.claim: He also glosses them as good speech.
THALABI:v6p174/r4.anchor: وروى عطية عن ابن عباس قال: هي الكلام الطيب.

THALABI:v6p174/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p174/r5.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v6p174/r5.claim: Intentions and aspirations are lasting deeds because actions are accepted and raised through them.
THALABI:v6p174/r5.anchor: قال عوف: سألت الحسن عن الباقيات الصالحات، قال: النيات والهمات

THALABI:v6p174/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p174/r6.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v6p174/r6.claim: He includes every act intended for God’s approval.
THALABI:v6p174/r6.anchor: قال قتادة: هي كل ما أريد به وجه الله.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r3.claim: Al-Farisi connects ولد with wealth and children, citing Quranic pairings of المال and البنون or الأولاد.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي: الولد: هو ما ذكر في التنزيل في غير موضع مع المال، قال: المال والبنون زينة الحياة الدنيا [الكهف/ 46]

NASHR:v1p359/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p359/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p359/r1.claim: Al-Azraq has six permissible connected-reading combinations for al-ān when the hamza of connection is replaced with alif.
NASHR:v1p359/r1.anchor: للأزرق في الآن ستة أوجه ... على وجه إبدال لدى وصله تجري

NASHR:v1p359/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p359/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p359/r2.claim: Three combinations disallowed in connection are allowed at pause; the six combinations require substitution, while facilitation permits three options for the second alif.
NASHR:v1p359/r2.anchor: وقولي لدى وصله قيد ليعلم أن وقفه ليس كذلك، فإن هذه الأوجه الثلاثة الممتنعة حالة الوصل تجوز

NASHR:v1p359/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p359/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p359/r3.claim: Full madd is apparent in al-Shatibi and al-Hudhali and possible in al-Unwan; tawassut comes by Abu al-Fath Faris in al-Taysir and is also apparent in al-Shatibi.
NASHR:v1p359/r3.anchor: (المد) وهو ظاهر كلام الشاطبي وكلام الهذيل

NASHR:v1p359/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p359/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p359/r4.claim: Qasr is rare on al-Azraq because Ibn Ghalbun and Ibn Bulayma transmit qasr in Amin but use substitution for hamzat al-wasl; it is explicit for al-Asbahani from Warsh, Qalun, and Abu Ja'far.
NASHR:v1p359/r4.anchor: (والقصر) وهو غريب في طريق الأزرق ; لأن أبا الحسن طاهر بن غلبون

NASHR:v1p359/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p359/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p359/r5.claim: When linking Alif-Lam-Mim, readers may use madd or qasr on the yāʾ of mīm according to whether the apparent madd is retained or the incidental factor counted.
NASHR:v1p359/r5.anchor: (الثامن) إذا قرئ (الم) بالوصل جاز لكل من القراء في الياء

NASHR:v1p359/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p359/r6.speaker: إسماعيل بن عبد الله النخاس ومحمد بن عمر بن خيرون
NASHR:v1p359/r6.claim: Al-Nahhas and Ibn Khayrun transmit from Warsh a no-madd option in alif-lam-mim; al-Dani says both options are good, and Makki and Abu al-Abbas also record both.
NASHR:v1p359/r6.anchor: وممن نص على ترك المد إسماعيل بن عبد الله النخاس، ومحمد بن عمر بن خيرون القيرواني، عن أصحابهما

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r1.claim: The hills are invoked for their relative nearness to rain-bearing clouds, not their height; valleys lack the same proximity to the clouds’ bounty.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r1.anchor: لم يقصد من الربى إلى العلو ولكن إلى الدنو فقط وكذلك لم يرد بذكر الوهاد الضعة والتسفل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r2.claim: A veiled sky is a plausible cause for hope of rain, conventionally treated as bounty and beneficence from the sky.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r2.anchor: فإستتار السماء بالغيم هو سبب رجاء الغيث الذي يعد في مجرى العادة جودا منها ونعمة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r3.speaker: إبن المعتز
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r3.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz supports the rain-as-gift image by describing the sky’s blessing on earth and the meadows’ gratitude for rain.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r3.anchor: كما قال إبن المعتز ( ما ترى نعمة السماء على الأر ض وشكر الرياض للأمطار )

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r4.claim: A praise trope claims that a quality seemingly innate in an object actually derives from the patron, as when sun and musk borrow light and fragrance.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r4.anchor: إن الشمس تستعير منه النور وتستفيده أو تتعلم منه الإشراق وتكتسب منه الإضاءة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r5.speaker: إبن بابك
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r5.claim: Ibn Bābak calls the garden breeze stolen from the patron and its description appropriated, while contrasting the patron’s faithful love with the garden’s fickleness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r5.anchor: ومن أخلاقه قال إبن بابك ( ألا يا رياض الحزن من أبرق الحمى نسيمك مسروق ووصفك منتحل )

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r6.claim: Another praise device invents a cause for a fixed feature of something in order to magnify the patron or another admired subject.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r6.anchor: يدعي في الصفة الثابتة للشيء أنه إنما كان لعلة يضعها الشاعر ويختلقها إما لأمر يرجع إلى تعظيم الممدوح

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r7.claim: A translated Persian couplet imagines Gemini wearing its belt to serve the patron; Jurjānī distinguishes this invented cause from escalating a simile into hyperbole.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p240/r7.anchor: لو لم تكن نية الجوزاء خدمته لما رأيت عليها عقد منتطق

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p360/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p360/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p360/r1.claim: Jurjānī juxtaposes al-Mutanabbī’s lines on a lover’s submission with a modern poet’s advice to submit for love, as paired poetic treatments of the theme.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p360/r1.anchor: تذلل لها واخضع على القرب والنوى فما عاشق من لا يذل ويخضع

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p360/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p360/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p360/r2.claim: In the second group, Jurjānī says the cited pairs display craft, imagery, and mastery; examples include Labīd, Nāfiʿ b. Laqīṭ, an unnamed Khārijite captive, Abū Tammām, and al-Nābigha.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p360/r2.anchor: ذكر ما أنت ترى فيه في كل واحد من البيتين صنعة وتصويرا وأستاذية على الجملة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p339/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p339/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p339/r1.claim: Adornment is whatever beautifies something and thereby makes the self desire it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p339/r1.anchor: الزينة ما يحصل به التحسين للشيء حتى تتوق النفس إليه بالشهوة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p339/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p339/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p339/r2.claim: One Qur'anic sense of zīna is beauty or beautification, as in the adorned worldly life, desirable passions, and the lamps of heaven.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p339/r2.anchor: أحدها : الحسن . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة : ﴿ زين للذين كفروا الحياة الدنيا ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p339/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p339/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p339/r3.claim: A second sense is jewelry or ornaments, as in the ornaments taken from Pharaoh's people.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p339/r3.anchor: والثاني : الحلي . ومنه قوله تعالى في طه : ﴿ ولكنا حملنا أوزارا من زينة القوم فقذفناها ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p339/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p339/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p339/r4.claim: A third sense is worldly display or luxury, including Pharaoh's wealth and the money and children that adorn worldly life.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p339/r4.anchor: والثالث : الزهرة . ومنه قوله تعالى في يونس : ﴿ ربنا إنك آتيت فرعون وملأه زينة وأموالا ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p339/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p339/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p339/r5.claim: A fourth sense is a retinue or display of attendants, as in the account of Qarun going out among his people in his finery.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p339/r5.anchor: والرابع : الحشم . ومنه قوله تعالى في القصص : ﴿ فخرج على قومه في زينته ﴾

BURHAN:v3p271/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p271/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p271/r1.claim: Arabic places the singular before the plural: wealth comes before sons when both are singular; when wealth is expressed as plural heaps, it follows sons.
BURHAN:v3p271/r1.anchor: سابق على الجمع كقوله تعالى ﴿ المال والبنون ﴾ وقوله ﴿ من مال وبنين ﴾

ITQAN:v4p520/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p520/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p520/r3.claim: Abu Saʿid reports that the lasting good deeds are takbir, tahlil, tasbih, praise of God, and saying there is no might or power except through God.
ITQAN:v4p520/r3.anchor: أخرج أحمد عنه أيضا عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال / الباقيات الصالحات / التكبير والتهليل والتسبيح والحمد لله ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله

ITQAN:v4p520/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p520/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p520/r4.claim: A second report from Abu Saʿid gives the lasting good deeds as glorifying, praising, declaring God’s oneness, and magnifying God.
ITQAN:v4p520/r4.anchor: وأخرجا عنه أيضا عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ITQAN:v4p520/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p520/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p520/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī transmits a similar raised report from Saʿd ibn Junadah identifying the lasting good deeds with these four phrases.
ITQAN:v4p520/r5.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني مثله من حديث سعد بن جنادة

ITQAN:v4p520/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p520/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p520/r6.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits from Abu Hurayra a Prophetic report that glorifying, praising, declaring God’s oneness, and magnifying God are among the lasting good deeds.
ITQAN:v4p520/r6.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر من الباقيات الصالحات )

ITQAN:v2p318/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p318/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p318/r8.claim: The lasting good deeds are remembrance of God.

DAMGHANI:v1p93/r18.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p93/r18.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p93/r18.claim: Thawāb means recompense or reward, as in the lasting deeds being better in reward.
DAMGHANI:v1p93/r18.anchor: فوجه منها الثواب بمعنى الجزاء قوله تعالى في سورة الكهف هو خير ثوابا يعني خير جزاء

DAMGHANI:v1p75/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p75/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p75/r5.claim: Al-bāqiyāt al-ṣāliḥāt can mean the five daily prayers.
DAMGHANI:v1p75/r5.anchor: البقية الصلوات الخمس . قوله تعالى في سورة الكهف ومريم
